questions.stem: Two jobs update the same warehouse table at the same time and one fails with an update conflict under snapshot isolation. What should you do?

options.text: Drop the table
Retry the failed transaction, or run the jobs so they don't update the same table at the same time
Switch the warehouse to read uncommitted
Disable transactions

questions.explanation: Fabric warehouse transactions use snapshot isolation, and concurrent updates to the same table can conflict. Retry, or schedule writers so they don't overlap.

questions.stem: A CREATE TABLE statement fails in a Fabric warehouse because of a column's data type datetime. What should you use instead?

options.text: timestamp
datetime2
sql_variant
text

questions.explanation: The warehouse supports a subset of SQL Server types; datetime isn't one of them and datetime2 is the supported replacement.

questions.stem: A query fails when some text values can't be converted to int. You want those rows to give NULL instead of failing the query. What do you use?

options.text: CAST(value AS int)
CONVERT(int, value)
ISNUMERIC(value) AS int
TRY_CAST(value AS int)

questions.explanation: TRY_CAST returns NULL when a conversion fails. CAST and CONVERT raise an error.

questions.stem: You need to find which warehouse queries failed last night and what they ran. Where do you look?

options.text: The OneLake catalog
The Spark UI
The queryinsights views, which keep a history of completed requests
The eventstream runtime logs

questions.explanation: Query insights keeps a history of completed requests on the warehouse, which is where you look for failed or canceled queries.

questions.stem: Connections to a Fabric warehouse that worked yesterday now fail, with no change to permissions, firewall or network. The error looks transient. What is the recommended first approach?

options.text: Retry the command in a tight loop immediately
Wait 5 to 10 minutes, open a new connection, then retry the command
Recreate the warehouse from a backup
Disable V-Order on the warehouse

questions.explanation: For transient errors, the guidance is not to retry immediately but to wait 5 to 10 minutes, establish a new connection and retry; most reconfiguration events finish in under 60 seconds.

questions.stem: A large warehouse query fails because tempdb runs out of space. Which change to the query is recommended?

options.text: Reduce the number of GROUP BY and ORDER BY columns if possible
Turn off result set caching
Wrap the query in an explicit transaction
Add more columns to the SELECT list

questions.explanation: Queries can fail when tempdb runs out of space; the steps include updating statistics, reducing GROUP BY and ORDER BY columns, and rerunning when nothing else runs.

questions.stem: A SELECT in a warehouse runs for a long time and then fails with no data returned to the client. You want to find out whether the backend query or the client side is the problem. What should you do?

options.text: Run UPDATE STATISTICS on every table
Run the same SELECT as a CTAS into another table in the same warehouse
Add OPTION (MAXDOP 1) to the query
Rerun the query with SET NOCOUNT ON

questions.explanation: A CTAS sends the result to a table instead of the client. If it succeeds and fills the table, the original failure is likely caused by the front end or the client.

questions.stem: Before you open a support ticket for a failed warehouse query, which identifiers should you provide that are returned as messages when the query completes or fails?

options.text: The Statement ID and the Distributed request ID
The Request ID and the Session ID of the last dataflow refresh
The OperationId from .show ingestion failures
The Spark application ID and the Livy session ID

questions.explanation: The guidance asks for the warehouse's workspace ID, the Statement ID and Distributed request ID, the exact error text and the time. The other IDs belong to Spark, dataflows and KQL.

questions.stem: Which two situations can cause a write-write (update) conflict in a Fabric warehouse? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: A session reads a view while another session creates statistics
One transaction DELETEs from a table while another UPDATEs the same table
Two transactions INSERT into two different tables
Two sessions run SELECT queries on the same table at the same time
Two transactions MERGE into the same table at the same time

questions.explanation: Conflicts can happen when two transactions try to UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE or TRUNCATE the same table. Concurrent reads and writes to different tables don't cause them.

questions.stem: This statement fails in a Fabric warehouse: `CREATE TABLE dbo.Orders (OrderId bigint IDENTITY, OrderDate date) WITH (CLUSTER BY (OrderId));` Why?

options.text: CLUSTER BY only works with SELECT INTO
date columns aren't allowed in a table that uses data clustering
IDENTITY columns can't be used with CLUSTER BY
CLUSTER BY needs at least two columns

questions.explanation: An IDENTITY column can't be a clustering column, although the table can still be clustered on other columns. CLUSTER BY needs one to four columns, and SELECT INTO with clustering isn't supported.
